item.title: BSc Thesis
item.description:
Creating a game with dynamic difficulty and reinforcement learning.

Student: João Gabriel Basi Supervisor: Prof. Dr. Roberto Hirata Jr.

Introduction

Player versus environment (PvE) games, in contrast to player versus player (PvP) games, are games where the player fights several enemies controlled by artificial intelligences in order to fulfill the game’s objectives. In this style, developers commonly model enemies as autonomous agents, since they make decisions without human intervention.

The creation and balancing of agents occupies a good part of PvE game development, since a large portion of the game experience is provided by them. For the game to become interesting, it is desirable that the agents offer challenges easy enough so that the player does not get frustrated, hard enough so that they do not get bored, and that there are new challenges at each stage.

item.title: Global Game Jam 2019
item.description:
A 48-hour gobal game jam. IME hosted a site and we divided USPGameDev into two groups.

My group created “Mother’s home”, a game where you are a little creative kid that adventures through an imaginary maze in his house to play with his toys, but don’t want to get far from his mom.

The theme was “What home means to you?”, and the game explores how the house feels like an unknown place to the kid, as his mother is his real home.

item.title: Ludum Dare 43
item.description:
In this jam we made “Mechamorphosis”, a game where you are a rusty robot that was captured by an evil organization that wants to turn you and your friends into mechanical waste. The goal is to aquire new parts to yourself, defeat all the guard robots and escape the building.

The theme was “Sacrifices must be made”, we created a mechanic where you have to sacrifice a part and get a new one to get to the next room. Some parts give you buffs and other debuffs, and you have to deal with them through the game.

item.title: Pirate Ship Battles
item.description:
An io-like online multiplayer, where you control a pirate ship and have to shoot other people’s ships to destroy them. It’s a browser game, that can be played either from desktop or from mobile devices.

The project had two phases. I contributed a lot for the first one, but after that it was used as an agile methodology classes’ project, that I was not enrolled, so I stopped contributing to it and started supporting the other developers’s work.

item.title: Ludum Dare 41
item.description:
We made “It’s all about lasagna!”, a farming game with a terror mood, where a kid goes to their grandma’s house and decides to make a lasagna while she doesn’t arrive.

The theme was “Combine two incompatible genres”, and we combined the peaceful and harmless life at the farm with the mood of a terror movie.

item.title: Ludum Dare 40
item.description:
We made “L.A.V.A. series L.A.M.P. edition vs the world”, a cyberpunk shooter, where the goal is to kill as many waves of monsters you can, using dozens of different weapons.

This edition’s theme was “The more you have, the worse it is”. You get a new weapon after each wave, and have to assign each one to a different key in the keyboard. As the time passes it gets harder to remember were each weapon was.

item.title: Livre Game Jam 2017
item.description:
A 48-hour game jam organized by LivreCamp, Gamux and Fellowship of the game to promote the use of free software. Our team from USPGameDev went to UNICAMP to participate.

We made the game “Network Battle: Chain Hostility”, an assimetric multiplayer game about a cyberwar between a hacker and the government.

The jam had the 4 themes listed below, from which the the groups had to choose two.

  • Less is more
  • Viral
  • Links
  • Privacy

It also had 9 achievements, from which our group won two of them

item.title: Derivative Calculator
item.description:

It is not optmized, so you may have to do some algebraic manipulations to simplify the result.
